abstract: Type I CRISPR-Cas systems couple RNA-guided target recognition to DNA degradation by a Cas3 nuclease-helicase. However, how initial nicking of the displaced non-target strand (NTS) at the active site of the Cas3 HD nuclease domain is coordinated with its subsequent loading into the helicase module remains poorly understood. Here, we report cryo-electron microscopy structures of the canonical type I-F surveillance complex (Csy) from Vibrio parahaemolyticus in DNA-unbound and DNA-bound states, together with two Csy-DNA-Cas2/3 structures consistent with states before and after initial NTS cleavage. Target DNA binding elongates the Csy complex and repositions the Cas8 helical bundle domain, creating a Cas2/3 recruitment platform involving Cas8 and Cas5. Cas2/3 captures a flexible NTS segment as a bulge at its HD nuclease active site, where an open RecA1 gate loop permits substrate access. Comparison of the two Cas2/3-bound structures suggests that, following initial nicking, the PAM-proximal NTS product disengages from the Cas8 helical bundle domain and is redirected into the helicase channel. Together with biochemical analyses, these structures provide a mechanistic framework for understanding how initial nicking is coupled to loading of the cleaved NTS into the helicase channel in type I CRISPR-Cas systems.
